---
title: Map your site's routes
description: If your docs link by published URL rather than file path, moose-kg cannot resolve those links until you tell it how routes map back to source files — and the broken links that remain afterwards are the ones worth fixing.
---

import { Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard, Steps, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

You ran `moose-kg stats` and got a long list of broken internal links that are not broken — they
work fine on your published site. Your corpus links by route, and moose-kg resolved those links
against the filesystem.

By the end of this page those links will be real graph edges, and the broken-link list will
contain only links that are actually broken.

## Before you start

You need a `graph.ttl` and a broken-link list from [`moose-kg stats`](/moose-kg/build/). Keep the
current count — you will compare against it.

## Why this is not automatic

A page writes `[find](/docs/actions/find)`. Your site generator publishes that correctly because
it knows `/docs/actions/find` is served from `src/content/docs/actions/find.mdx`. That mapping
lives in the generator's config, in a convention, or in both.

moose-kg does not read your generator's config — it would need one adapter per generator, and they
change. It takes the mapping from you instead, once.

## Configure the mapping

A route entry answers two questions: what URL prefix the site serves, and which repo directory
serves it.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Astro / Starlight">
    ```yaml title="moose.config.yaml"
    routes:
      - basePath: /docs
        root: src/content/docs
        extensions: [".md", ".mdx"]
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Docusaurus">
    ```yaml title="moose.config.yaml"
    routes:
      - basePath: /docs
        root: docs
        extensions: [".md", ".mdx"]
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="MkDocs">
    ```yaml title="moose.config.yaml"
    routes:
      - basePath: /
        root: docs
        extensions: [".md"]
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `root` | **required** | The repo directory the route serves. |
| `basePath` | `/` | The URL prefix. Normalized to a leading `/` with no trailing `/`; `/` means site root. |
| `extensions` | `[".md", ".mdx"]` | Tried in order when the URL has no extension. |
| `indexFiles` | `["index", "README"]` | Resolves a directory URL like `/docs/actions/`. |

So `/docs/actions/find` becomes `src/content/docs/actions/find.mdx`, and `/docs/actions/` becomes
`src/content/docs/actions/index.mdx`.

## Multiple routes are normal

A docs section and a blog usually publish under different prefixes from different directories.
List them all; each is matched independently.

```yaml title="moose.config.yaml"
kg:
  routes:
    - basePath: /docs
      root: src/content/docs
    - basePath: /blog
      root: src/content/blog
```

<Aside type="note" title="Route mappings are config-only">
  There is no CLI flag. Routes define what the corpus *means*, so a graph built with different
  route rules is a different graph — it should not vary with how someone typed the command.
</Aside>

## Verify by delta

<Steps>

1. **Rebuild and re-run stats.**

   ```sh
   moose-kg build && moose-kg stats
   ```

   The broken-link count should drop sharply. If it does not move at all, your `root` probably
   does not match where the files actually live.

2. **Inspect one edge rather than trusting the number.**

   ```sh
   moose-kg query -p dcterms:references
   ```

   Confirm a link you know is route-style now points at the source file you expect.

</Steps>

## The remaining broken links are the point

This is the outcome worth caring about. Before mapping, the broken-link list was noise you had to
ignore. After mapping, everything left in it is a link that genuinely resolves to nothing —
usually a page that was moved or deleted without its inbound links being updated.

That list is now small enough to act on, and stable enough to
[gate on in CI](/moose-kg/govern/ci/).

<Aside type="note" title="Route mapping applies to component links too">
  A route written as `<LinkCard href="/docs/actions/find" />` in an `.mdx` file resolves through the
  same mapping as a Markdown link. If your site is component-heavy, expect the broken-link count to
  move substantially the first time you configure routes.
</Aside>

## What you have now

Site-style links resolved to real `dcterms:references` edges, impact analysis that reflects how
your documentation actually cross-references itself, and a broken-link count that means something.
